title: Synthesis standup: leads roundup and cross-team actions
summary: Consolidated weekly sync for cross-team engineering leadership. Focus: unblock Dedicated rollout ops, prioritize runtime perf regressions surfaced in last week's canary, and finalize observability retention proposal before exec review. Capture decisions and concrete owners for next-sprint actions.
agenda: Quick pulse: top risk per team (2m each)
Dedicated rollout status and capacity contingency
API backward-compatibility check for streaming changes
attendees: Alex Romero (Release Eng - joined for rollout section)
meeting_notes: - Platform: Maya: Dedicated capacity onboarding for Beta-Cust-3 delayed by NVMe provisioning (vendor ETA 3 business days). Workaround: soft-capacity throttling and schedule priority lanes for pre-warmed instances.
- Serving Runtime: Diego: Canary showed 6-8% p99 latency increase on long-context paths after last microkernel swap. Observed underutilized memory compaction causing more GC pauses.
- Observability: Evelyn: retention proposal (60d vs 30d) will increase infra cost ~14% but enables end-to-end incident forensics; need exec signoff by Friday.
- Private Deployments: Priya: compliance checklist awaiting customer SOC2 attestation artifact; legal expects artifact by 2028-03-20 to meet customer TAM timeline.
- SRE: Owen: small uptick in transient replication lag in west-2 region tied to a storage firmware update; ops mitigation in place, monitoring alert threshold lowered temporarily.
- Product: Lina: internal API change for streaming structured events requires backward-compatibility gating; product wants a grace period feature flag for 6 weeks.
deep_dive_serving_runtime: - Symptom: p95->p99 tail widening by 6-8% on requests with sequence length>4096 since kernel swap (2028-03-10 deploy).
- Investigation notes: memory compaction heuristics changed; KV-cache eviction jitter increased; not reproducing on x86 CPU nodes, isolated to Ampere GPU fleet under high-concurrency workloads.
- Immediate mitigation: roll forward to previous kernel on a subset of canary nodes (Diego to coordinate) and increase async-prefetch cooldown to reduce eviction churn.
- Risk: if kernel rollback delayed >48h, customer A/B tests may show error spikes—tie-breaker: prioritize rollback if any customer-facing anomaly appears.

- Next steps: run micro-bench harness across GPU types (Diego + release eng), add targeted e2e test with long-sequence synthetic traces (QA + runtime), and instrument per-request KV-cache evictions (observability).
dedicated_rollout_notes: - Beta-Cust-3 onboarding hit by NVMe procurement. Delivery SLA updated; expected cutover 2028-03-20.
- Contingency: use 'pre-warm lanes' with smaller instance profile and aggressive prefix caching to simulate capacity while hardware arrives.
- Action: Alex to prepare rollout playbook variant for soft-capacity (includes traffic shaping, priority lanes, customer comms).
observability_retention: - 60d retention provides conviction for regression alerts and prompt-level replay for eval pipelines, cost +14% (Evelyn provided granular cost model).
- Compromise option: 90d retention for token-level aggregates only + 30d for full traces (cost +7%).
- Decision: present both options to exec on Friday; recommendation to pursue 60d if legal/compliance flags low, otherwise fallback to hybrid option.
decisions: 1) Rollback of microkernel on canary nodes is authorized immediately if any customer-facing errors are observed; otherwise proceed with measured rollback on 20% canary cluster to validate (Diego owns execution).
2) Observability retention proposal: present both full-60d and hybrid options to Exec; Platform leadership recommends full-60d pending legal review (Maya + Evelyn to prep slides).
3) Soft-capacity rollout playbook variant approved for Dedicated Beta-Cust-3 (Alex to ship playbook).
4) Feature flag for streaming API deprecation: allow 6-week grace period; Product + SDK teams to coordinate compatibility shims (Lina + DevEx).
